blocks.en: "Therefore whoever confesses Me before men, him I will also confess before My Father who is in heaven." — Matthew 10:32 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Cualquiera, pues, que me confiese delante de los hombres, le confesaré yo también delante de mi Padre que está en los cielos." — Mateo 10:32

blocks.en: The King Sends His Messengers
blocks.es_reference: El Rey Envía a Sus Mensajeros

blocks.en: Up to this point the King has been gathering disciples to Himself; now He sends them out. "And when He had called His twelve disciples to Him, He gave them power over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all kinds of sickness" (Matthew 10:1). The King who came preaching the kingdom now multiplies His voice, entrusting His own authority to twelve ordinary men. Their first commission is narrow: "Go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel" (Matthew 10:6), and their message is the same word John and Jesus both preached — "The kingdom of heaven is at hand" (Matthew 10:7). They are to give as freely as they have received, carrying no gold and no extra provision, depending wholly on the One who sent them. From the start the mission is not a human enterprise to be managed but a trust to be carried in dependence on God.
blocks.es_reference: Hasta aquí el Rey ha estado reuniendo discípulos para sí; ahora los envía. "Entonces llamando a sus doce discípulos, les dio potestad contra los espíritus inmundos, para que los echasen fuera, y para sanar toda enfermedad y toda dolencia" (Mateo 10:1). El Rey que vino predicando el reino ahora multiplica su voz, confiando su propia autoridad a doce hombres comunes. Su primera comisión es estrecha: "Id antes a las ovejas perdidas de la casa de Israel" (Mateo 10:6), y su mensaje es la misma palabra que predicaron Juan y Jesús — "El reino de los cielos se ha acercado" (Mateo 10:7). Han de dar tan gratuitamente como han recibido, sin llevar oro ni provisión de más, dependiendo enteramente de Aquel que los envió. Desde el principio la misión no es una empresa humana que administrar sino un encargo que llevar en dependencia de Dios.

blocks.en: Sheep Among Wolves
blocks.es_reference: Ovejas en Medio de Lobos

blocks.en: But Jesus does not send them out with false comfort. "Behold, I send you out as sheep in the midst of wolves. Therefore be wise as serpents and harmless as doves" (Matthew 10:16). He tells them plainly that they will be handed over to councils, dragged before governors, and hated for His name's sake — "but he who endures to the end will be saved" (Matthew 10:22). This is the first clear note of the opposition that will rise through these chapters and finally crest at the cross. And yet, three times in this passage, the King says, "Do not fear." Do not fear those who can kill the body but cannot touch the soul. Are not two sparrows sold for a copper coin, and not one of them falls to the ground apart from your Father's will? "But the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Do not fear therefore; you are of more value than many sparrows" (Matthew 10:30-31). The messengers go into danger, but they go watched over by a Father to whom no sparrow and no servant is small.
blocks.es_reference: Pero Jesús no los envía con falso consuelo. "He aquí, yo os envío como a ovejas en medio de lobos; sed, pues, prudentes como serpientes, y sencillos como palomas" (Mateo 10:16). Les dice claramente que serán entregados a concilios, llevados ante gobernadores y aborrecidos por causa de su nombre — "mas el que persevere hasta el fin, éste será salvo" (Mateo 10:22). Esta es la primera nota clara de la oposición que se levantará a lo largo de estos capítulos y que al fin culminará en la cruz. Y sin embargo, tres veces en este pasaje, el Rey dice: "No temáis." No temáis a los que matan el cuerpo mas no pueden tocar el alma. ¿No se venden dos pajarillos por una moneda, y ni uno de ellos cae a tierra sin la voluntad de vuestro Padre? "Pues aun vuestros cabellos están todos contados. Así que, no temáis; más valéis vosotros que muchos pajarillos" (Mateo 10:30-31). Los mensajeros van al peligro, pero van guardados por un Padre para quien ningún pajarillo y ningún siervo es pequeño.

blocks.en: The Marks of a Disciple
blocks.es_reference: Las Marcas de un Discípulo

blocks.en: Then Jesus turns from the mission to the disciple himself, and lays down what it costs to belong to Him. The first mark is confession: "Whoever confesses Me before men, him I will also confess before My Father who is in heaven. But whoever denies Me before men, him I will also deny before My Father" (Matthew 10:32-33). A true disciple sees the King clearly enough to own Him out loud, in a world that would rather he kept silent. The second mark is love that outranks every rival: "He who loves father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me" (Matthew 10:37). Jesus is not setting family aside as worthless; He is claiming the first place that belongs to God alone. So He warns that following Him may bring a sword rather than easy peace — division even within a household (Matthew 10:34-36) — because a loyalty this total will always cut across lesser loyalties. The third mark is the cross: "He who does not take his cross and follow after Me is not worthy of Me. He who finds his life will lose it, and he who loses his life for My sake will find it" (Matthew 10:38-39). To follow the King nearly is to die to self and find true life in Him. See Him clearly, love Him dearly, follow Him nearly — that is the shape of a disciple's life.
blocks.es_reference: Entonces Jesús pasa de la misión al discípulo mismo, y establece lo que cuesta pertenecerle. La primera marca es la confesión: "Cualquiera, pues, que me confiese delante de los hombres, le confesaré yo también delante de mi Padre que está en los cielos. Y a cualquiera que me niegue delante de los hombres, le negaré yo también delante de mi Padre" (Mateo 10:32-33). Un verdadero discípulo ve al Rey con suficiente claridad como para reconocerlo en voz alta, en un mundo que preferiría que callara. La segunda marca es un amor que sobrepasa a todo rival: "El que ama a padre o madre más que a mí, no es digno de mí" (Mateo 10:37). Jesús no aparta a la familia como cosa sin valor; reclama el primer lugar que pertenece a Dios solo. Por eso advierte que seguirle puede traer espada antes que paz fácil — división aun dentro de una casa (Mateo 10:34-36) — porque una lealtad tan total siempre cortará a través de lealtades menores. La tercera marca es la cruz: "Y el que no toma su cruz y sigue en pos de mí, no es digno de mí. El que halla su vida, la perderá; y el que pierde su vida por causa de mí, la hallará" (Mateo 10:38-39). Seguir de cerca al Rey es morir a sí mismo y hallar la verdadera vida en Él. Verle con claridad, amarle de veras, seguirle de cerca — esa es la forma de la vida de un discípulo.

blocks.en: A Mark That Shows Whose We Are
blocks.es_reference: Una Marca Que Muestra de Quién Somos

blocks.en: In an earlier sermon on this passage I used an old family branding iron stamped with the name Cook. My father had used it on cattle, and the mark told everyone who they belonged to. Jesus says that a disciple also bears recognizable marks. The sermon gathered them under three headings: commitment, confession, and cost. Commitment is more than interest in God; it becomes active service. Confession is more than a private opinion; Christ is owned with the lips and displayed by the influence of a changed life. And discipleship has a cost: family loyalties, worldly interests, and even life itself can never outrank the Lord. The old stagecoach illustration makes the point memorably. First-class passengers kept their seats on the steep hill, second-class passengers got out and walked, but third-class passengers got out and pushed. The church needs disciples who will push — not from guilt, but from love. Jesus' words in Matthew 10 therefore ask not merely whether we admire Him, but whether His ownership is visible on us.
blocks.es_reference: En un sermón anterior sobre este pasaje usé un viejo hierro de marcar de la familia con el apellido Cook. Mi padre lo había usado para marcar el ganado, y la marca decía a todos a quién pertenecía. Jesús enseña que un discípulo también lleva marcas reconocibles. El sermón las reunió bajo tres encabezados: compromiso, confesión y costo. El compromiso es más que interés en Dios; se convierte en servicio activo. La confesión es más que una opinión privada; reconocemos a Cristo con los labios y lo mostramos mediante la influencia de una vida cambiada. Y el discipulado tiene un costo: las lealtades familiares, los intereses del mundo y aun la vida misma nunca pueden ocupar un lugar por encima del Señor. La antigua ilustración de la diligencia lo expresa bien. Los pasajeros de primera clase permanecían sentados al subir una cuesta; los de segunda bajaban y caminaban; pero los de tercera bajaban y empujaban. La iglesia necesita discípulos que empujen — no por culpa, sino por amor. Por eso Mateo 10 no pregunta solamente si admiramos a Jesús, sino si Su marca de propiedad puede verse en nosotros.

blocks.en: Are You the Coming One?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Eres Tú el Que Había de Venir?

blocks.en: Now the scene shifts to a prison cell. John the Baptist, the bold herald of Unit 2, sits in Herod's prison, and doubt steals in. He sends his own disciples to ask Jesus, "Are You the Coming One, or do we look for another?" (Matthew 11:3). It is a tender and honest question, and Jesus does not rebuke it. He answers by pointing to His works: "The blind see and the lame walk; the lepers are cleansed and the deaf hear; the dead are raised up and the poor have the gospel preached to them. And blessed is he who is not offended because of Me" (Matthew 11:5-6). The signs Isaiah promised of the kingdom are happening in plain sight. Then Jesus honors John before the crowd, calling him the greatest born of women — and yet adds a startling word: "He who is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he" (Matthew 11:11). So great is the kingdom now breaking in that the least within it stands on ground the prophets only longed to see.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora la escena se traslada a una celda. Juan el Bautista, el osado heraldo de la Unidad 2, está en la cárcel de Herodes, y la duda se cuela. Envía a sus propios discípulos a preguntar a Jesús: "¿Eres tú aquel que había de venir, o esperaremos a otro?" (Mateo 11:3). Es una pregunta tierna y honesta, y Jesús no la reprende. Responde señalando sus obras: "Los ciegos ven, y los cojos andan; los leprosos son limpiados, y los sordos oyen; los muertos son resucitados, y a los pobres es anunciado el evangelio. Y bienaventurado es el que no se ofendiere en mí" (Mateo 11:5-6). Las señales que Isaías prometió del reino están sucediendo a la vista de todos. Luego Jesús honra a Juan ante la multitud, llamándolo el mayor de los nacidos de mujer — y sin embargo añade una palabra asombrosa: "El más pequeño en el reino de los cielos, mayor es que él" (Mateo 11:11). Tan grande es el reino que ahora irrumpe, que el más pequeño dentro de él pisa terreno que los profetas solo anhelaron ver.

blocks.en: Come to Me
blocks.es_reference: Venid a Mí

blocks.en: The opposition deepens. Jesus pronounces woes on the cities that saw His mighty works and would not repent — Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum, His own adopted town — warning that it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon, even for Sodom, in the day of judgment than for them (Matthew 11:20-24). The greater the light refused, the heavier the account. And yet from the same lips, in the same hour, comes the gentlest invitation in all the Gospels: "Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For My yoke is easy and My burden is light" (Matthew 11:28-30). The King who warns the hard-hearted opens His arms to the weary. His rule is not another load piled on tired backs; it is rest for the soul.
blocks.es_reference: La oposición se ahonda. Jesús pronuncia ayes sobre las ciudades que vieron sus grandes obras y no se arrepintieron — Corazín, Betsaida y Capernaum, su propia ciudad adoptiva — advirtiendo que será más tolerable para Tiro y Sidón, y aun para Sodoma, en el día del juicio que para ellas (Mateo 11:20-24). Mientras mayor es la luz rechazada, más pesada es la cuenta. Y sin embargo de los mismos labios, en la misma hora, viene la más tierna invitación de todos los Evangelios: "Venid a mí todos los que estáis trabajados y cargados, y yo os haré descansar. Llevad mi yugo sobre vosotros, y aprended de mí, que soy manso y humilde de corazón; y hallaréis descanso para vuestras almas. Porque mi yugo es fácil, y ligera mi carga" (Mateo 11:28-30). El Rey que advierte a los de corazón duro abre sus brazos a los cansados. Su reinado no es otra carga amontonada sobre espaldas fatigadas; es descanso para el alma.

blocks.en: Lord of the Sabbath
blocks.es_reference: Señor del Día de Reposo

blocks.en: In chapter 12 the rising opposition takes sharper form, and the battleground is the Sabbath. When His disciples pluck heads of grain on the Sabbath because they are hungry, the Pharisees object, and Jesus answers them out of Scripture — David ate the showbread, the priests work in the temple — and declares, "I desire mercy and not sacrifice," and then, "the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath" (Matthew 12:7-8). Soon after, in the synagogue, He heals a man with a withered hand, asking which of them would not lift a sheep out of a pit on the Sabbath: "Of how much more value then is a man than a sheep? Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath" (Matthew 12:12). The Pharisees had buried the Sabbath under their own rules and lost its purpose; the King restores it as a gift for man's good. But their response shows where opposition is heading: "Then the Pharisees went out and plotted against Him, how they might destroy Him" (Matthew 12:14). Matthew sees even here the gentle Servant of Isaiah, who will not break a bruised reed nor quench a smoking flax (Matthew 12:20).
blocks.es_reference: En el capítulo 12 la oposición creciente toma forma más aguda, y el campo de batalla es el día de reposo. Cuando sus discípulos arrancan espigas en el día de reposo porque tienen hambre, los fariseos objetan, y Jesús les responde desde la Escritura — David comió los panes de la proposición, los sacerdotes trabajan en el templo — y declara: "Misericordia quiero, y no sacrificio," y luego: "el Hijo del Hombre es Señor aun del día de reposo" (Mateo 12:7-8). Poco después, en la sinagoga, sana a un hombre de la mano seca, preguntando cuál de ellos no sacaría una oveja de un hoyo en el día de reposo: "Pues ¿cuánto más vale un hombre que una oveja? Es, por tanto, lícito hacer el bien en los días de reposo" (Mateo 12:12). Los fariseos habían sepultado el día de reposo bajo sus propias reglas y habían perdido su propósito; el Rey lo restaura como un don para el bien del hombre. Pero su respuesta muestra hacia dónde va la oposición: "Y salidos los fariseos, tuvieron consejo contra él para destruirle" (Mateo 12:14). Mateo ve aun aquí al Siervo manso de Isaías, que no quebrará la caña cascada ni apagará el pábilo que humea (Mateo 12:20).

blocks.en: The Unpardonable Sin
blocks.es_reference: El Pecado Imperdonable

blocks.en: The conflict reaches its most solemn point when Jesus casts a demon out of a blind and mute man, and the Pharisees, unable to deny the miracle, attribute it to the devil: "This fellow does not cast out demons except by Beelzebub" (Matthew 12:24). Jesus shows the folly of it — a kingdom divided against itself cannot stand, and if He casts out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon them (Matthew 12:28). Here He draws the line that runs through the whole unit: "He who is not with Me is against Me" (Matthew 12:30). Then comes the gravest warning in Matthew: "Every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven men... either in this age or in the age to come" (Matthew 12:31-32). What is this unpardonable sin? It is not a single slip of the tongue. The Pharisees were looking straight at the Spirit's own work and calling it the devil's — knowing better, and hardening themselves against the only One who could lead them to repentance. Blasphemy against the Spirit is the settled, willful, final rejection of the Spirit's witness to Christ; it is the sin of unbelief carried to the point of no return. It cannot be forgiven, not because God's grace runs short, but because the man who persists in calling good evil has shut against himself the only door through which forgiveness comes. Let this comfort the troubled soul who fears having committed it: that very fear is the Spirit still at work, a tender conscience He has not abandoned. The man who has truly turned final against the Spirit no longer cares at all.
blocks.es_reference: El conflicto llega a su punto más solemne cuando Jesús echa un demonio de un hombre ciego y mudo, y los fariseos, incapaces de negar el milagro, lo atribuyen al diablo: "Éste no echa fuera los demonios sino por Beelzebú" (Mateo 12:24). Jesús muestra lo necio de ello — un reino dividido contra sí mismo no puede permanecer, y si Él echa fuera los demonios por el Espíritu de Dios, entonces el reino de Dios ha llegado a ellos (Mateo 12:28). Aquí traza la línea que recorre toda la unidad: "El que no es conmigo, contra mí es" (Mateo 12:30). Luego viene la advertencia más grave de Mateo: "Todo pecado y blasfemia será perdonado a los hombres; mas la blasfemia contra el Espíritu no les será perdonada... ni en este mundo, ni en el venidero" (Mateo 12:31-32). ¿Qué es este pecado imperdonable? No es un solo desliz de la lengua. Los fariseos miraban de frente la obra misma del Espíritu y la llamaban del diablo — sabiendo lo mejor, y endureciéndose contra el único que podía llevarlos al arrepentimiento. La blasfemia contra el Espíritu es el rechazo asentado, voluntario y final del testimonio del Espíritu acerca de Cristo; es el pecado de incredulidad llevado al punto sin retorno. No puede ser perdonado, no porque la gracia de Dios se agote, sino porque el hombre que persiste en llamar al bien mal ha cerrado contra sí mismo la única puerta por la que viene el perdón. Que esto consuele al alma turbada que teme haberlo cometido: ese mismo temor es el Espíritu obrando todavía, una conciencia tierna que Él no ha abandonado. El hombre que de veras se ha vuelto final contra el Espíritu ya no se preocupa en absoluto.

blocks.en: The Sign of Jonah
blocks.es_reference: La Señal de Jonás

blocks.en: When the scribes and Pharisees demand a sign, Jesus refuses to perform on command. "An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah. For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth" (Matthew 12:39-40). Here the King points past every lesser wonder to the one sign that will settle everything — His own death and resurrection. As Jonah came up from the deep as if from the grave, so the Son of Man will rise. This is the same pattern of fulfillment we have traced from the beginning: an old story of the prophet Jonah becomes a true sign of the greater work of Christ. Jesus warns that the men of Nineveh, who repented at Jonah's preaching, will rise in judgment against this generation, "for indeed a greater than Jonah is here" (Matthew 12:41).
blocks.es_reference: Cuando los escribas y fariseos exigen una señal, Jesús se niega a actuar por encargo. "La generación mala y adúltera demanda señal; mas señal no le será dada, sino la señal del profeta Jonás. Porque como estuvo Jonás en el vientre del gran pez tres días y tres noches, así estará el Hijo del Hombre en el corazón de la tierra tres días y tres noches" (Mateo 12:39-40). Aquí el Rey señala más allá de toda maravilla menor a la única señal que lo resolverá todo — su propia muerte y resurrección. Como Jonás salió de lo profundo como de la tumba, así resucitará el Hijo del Hombre. Este es el mismo patrón de cumplimiento que hemos trazado desde el principio: una vieja historia del profeta Jonás se vuelve una verdadera señal de la obra mayor de Cristo. Jesús advierte que los hombres de Nínive, que se arrepintieron a la predicación de Jonás, se levantarán en juicio contra esta generación, "porque he aquí más que Jonás en este lugar" (Mateo 12:41).

blocks.en: The True Family
blocks.es_reference: La Verdadera Familia

blocks.en: The unit closes with a quiet but searching scene. While Jesus is teaching, word comes that His mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak with Him. He answers with a question that redraws the lines of belonging: "Who is My mother and who are My brothers?" And stretching out His hand toward His disciples, He says, "Here are My mother and My brothers! For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother" (Matthew 12:48-50). The kingdom the messengers were sent to announce gathers a new family, bound not by blood but by obedience to the Father. The opposition has been rising — Pharisees plotting, cities refusing, the charge of Beelzebub — but around the King a people is forming who hear the will of God and do it.
blocks.es_reference: La unidad cierra con una escena callada pero penetrante. Mientras Jesús enseña, llega aviso de que su madre y sus hermanos están afuera, queriendo hablarle. Él responde con una pregunta que vuelve a trazar las líneas de la pertenencia: "¿Quién es mi madre, y quiénes son mis hermanos?" Y extendiendo su mano hacia sus discípulos, dice: "He aquí mi madre y mis hermanos. Porque todo aquel que hace la voluntad de mi Padre que está en los cielos, ése es mi hermano, y hermana, y madre" (Mateo 12:48-50). El reino que los mensajeros fueron enviados a anunciar reúne una nueva familia, unida no por la sangre sino por la obediencia al Padre. La oposición ha venido creciendo — fariseos conspirando, ciudades rechazando, la acusación de Beelzebú — pero alrededor del Rey se forma un pueblo que oye la voluntad de Dios y la hace.

blocks.en: Mission and Opposition
blocks.es_reference: Misión y Oposición

blocks.en: These three chapters move on two tracks at once. On one track the King's mission goes out — the Twelve are sent, the message spreads, the weary are invited, a new family is gathered. On the other track opposition rises — messengers are warned of wolves, cities refuse to repent, Pharisees plot His death and slander the Spirit's work. The two tracks are not really separate; the same light that draws some hardens others. And running down the middle is the line Jesus Himself drew: "He who is not with Me is against Me." There is no neutral ground before this King. The same word that sent the Twelve and welcomed the weary still asks each of us where we stand — with Him, confessing and following, or against Him. To do the will of the Father is to belong to His family forever.
blocks.es_reference: Estos tres capítulos avanzan por dos vías a la vez. En una vía la misión del Rey sale — los Doce son enviados, el mensaje se extiende, los cansados son invitados, una nueva familia es reunida. En la otra vía la oposición se levanta — los mensajeros son advertidos de lobos, las ciudades rehúsan arrepentirse, los fariseos traman su muerte y calumnian la obra del Espíritu. Las dos vías no están de veras separadas; la misma luz que atrae a unos endurece a otros. Y por el medio corre la línea que Jesús mismo trazó: "El que no es conmigo, contra mí es." No hay terreno neutral ante este Rey. La misma palabra que envió a los Doce y recibió a los cansados todavía nos pregunta a cada uno dónde estamos — con Él, confesando y siguiendo, o contra Él. Hacer la voluntad del Padre es pertenecer a su familia para siempre.

blocks.en: "For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother." — Matthew 12:50 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Porque todo aquel que hace la voluntad de mi Padre que está en los cielos, ése es mi hermano, y hermana, y madre." — Mateo 12:50 (RVG)

Si no aprueba, el examen espera un tiempo breve antes de intentarlo de nuevo.

mc.stem: From prison, John the Baptist sent disciples to ask Jesus:
options: Are You the Coming One, or do we look for another?
mc.why: John, in doubt, asked whether Jesus was truly the Coming One.

mc.stem: Jesus answered John's question by pointing to:
options: His works — the blind see, the lame walk, the poor hear the gospel
mc.why: The kingdom signs Isaiah promised were happening in plain view.

mc.stem: The invitation 'Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden' promises:
mc.why: His yoke is easy and His burden light; He gives rest for the soul.

mc.stem: In the Sabbath controversies, Jesus declared Himself to be:
mc.why: He taught that it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath, for He is its Lord.

mc.stem: After Jesus healed on the Sabbath, the Pharisees responded by:
options: Plotting how they might destroy Him
mc.why: Their plotting shows how the opposition was hardening toward His death.

mc.stem: When Jesus cast out a demon, the Pharisees claimed He did it by:
mc.why: Unable to deny the miracle, they attributed the Spirit's work to the devil.

mc.stem: Jesus said that if He cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then:
options: The kingdom of God had come upon them
mc.why: His casting out of demons by the Spirit was a sign the kingdom had arrived.

mc.stem: The line Jesus drew through this whole section is:
options: 'He who is not with Me is against Me'
mc.why: There is no neutral ground before this King — one is with Him or against Him.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, blasphemy against the Holy Spirit is best understood as:
options: The settled, willful, final rejection of the Spirit's witness to Christ
mc.why: It is the sin of unbelief carried to the point of no return, not a single slip.

mc.stem: The lesson offers this comfort to one who fears having committed the unpardonable sin:
options: It can be undone by penance
No one can ever be sure
That very fear shows the Spirit is still at work in a tender conscience
mc.why: Those who have truly committed it no longer care; the troubled soul's fear is itself a sign of grace.

mc.stem: When asked for a sign, Jesus said none would be given except:
options: The sign of the prophet Jonah
mc.why: As Jonah was three days in the fish, so the Son of Man would be in the heart of the earth.

mc.stem: The sign of Jonah points forward to Jesus':
mc.why: As Jonah came up from the deep, so the Son of Man would rise from the heart of the earth.

mc.stem: Jesus said that His true mother and brothers are those who:
options: Do the will of His Father in heaven
mc.why: The King's new family is bound not by blood but by obedience to the Father.

sa.prompt: Describe the mission Jesus gave the Twelve — whom He sent, with what authority, and what message.
sa.model: Jesus called His twelve disciples, the apostles, and gave them His own authority over unclean spirits and demons, to cast them out and to heal every sickness. He sent them first on a narrow mission, to the lost sheep of the house of Israel rather than to the Gentiles. Their message was the same word John and Jesus preached, that the kingdom of heaven is at hand. They were to give as freely as they had received, carrying no gold and no extra provision, so that the whole mission depended not on human resources but on the God who sent them. The King who came preaching the kingdom now multiplied His voice through these twelve ordinary men.

sa.prompt: What did Jesus warn would come to His messengers, and why did He say they need not be afraid?
sa.model: Jesus warned His messengers that He was sending them out as sheep in the midst of wolves; they would be handed over to councils and governors and would be hated for His name's sake, persecuted as He Himself would be. Yet He told them not to be afraid, three times over. They should not fear those who can kill the body but cannot touch the soul. He reminded them that not one sparrow falls to the ground apart from their Father's will, and that even the hairs of their head are all numbered. Because the Father watches over even the smallest sparrow, His servants who must endure persecution are never out of His sight or care.

sa.prompt: Set out the marks of a true disciple that Jesus gives in Matthew 10:32-39.
sa.model: The first mark of a disciple is confession: whoever confesses Christ before men, Christ will confess before the Father, but whoever denies Him will be denied. The second mark is a love for Christ that outranks every rival, so that the one who loves father or mother or family more than Him is not worthy of Him; this total loyalty may bring a sword and division rather than easy peace. The third mark is the cross: the disciple who does not take up his cross and follow after Christ is not worthy of Him, and the one who finds his life will lose it while the one losing his life for Christ's sake will find it. To follow the King is to see Him clearly, love Him dearly, and follow Him nearly, dying to self to find true life in Him.

sa.prompt: What did John the Baptist ask from prison, and how did Jesus answer him?
sa.model: From Herod's prison, John the Baptist, troubled by doubt, sent his own disciples with the question whether Jesus was the Coming One or whether they should look for another. Jesus did not rebuke the honest question. He answered by pointing to His works and miracles: the blind see and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed and the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have the gospel preached to them. These were the signs Isaiah had promised of the kingdom, happening in plain view. He added a gentle blessing on the one who is not offended because of Him, and then honored John before the crowd as the greatest born of women.

sa.prompt: To whom is the invitation 'Come to Me' addressed, and what does the King offer?
sa.model: In the same hour that He pronounced woes on the cities that would not repent, Jesus opened His arms with the gentlest invitation in the Gospels. It is addressed to all who labor and are heavy laden, the weary and the burdened. He calls them to come to Him and take His yoke upon them and learn from Him, for He is gentle and lowly in heart. What He offers is rest for their souls, because His yoke is easy and His burden is light. His rule is not another heavy load piled on tired backs; it is the rest that the weary cannot find anywhere else, given freely by a King who is gentle toward those who come to Him.

sa.prompt: Explain the Sabbath controversy and the claim Jesus made about Himself.
sa.model: When the disciples plucked heads of grain on the Sabbath because they were hungry, the Pharisees objected, and Jesus answered them from Scripture, recalling how David ate the showbread and how the priests work in the temple on the Sabbath. He declared that God desires mercy and not sacrifice, and that the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath. Then in the synagogue He healed a man with a withered hand, asking whether they would not lift a sheep out of a pit on the Sabbath, and teaching that it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath. The Pharisees had buried the day under their own rules and lost its purpose, but the King restored it as a gift for the good of man, even as they plotted against Him.

sa.prompt: What did the Pharisees charge when Jesus cast out a demon, and how did He answer?
sa.model: When Jesus cast a demon out of a blind and mute man, the Pharisees could not deny the miracle, so they charged that He cast out demons only by Beelzebub, the ruler of the demons. Jesus exposed the folly of the charge: a kingdom or house divided against itself cannot stand, and Satan would not be casting out Satan. He told them that if He cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God had come upon them. Here He drew the line that runs through the whole section, that the one who is not with Him is against Him. To attribute the obvious work of the Spirit to the devil was to set oneself deliberately against the very power of God at work before their eyes.

sa.prompt: What is blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, and why does the lesson say it cannot be forgiven?
sa.model: Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit is not a single careless word but the settled, willful, and final rejection of the Spirit's witness to Christ. The Pharisees were looking straight at the Spirit's own work and calling it the devil's, knowing better and hardening themselves against the only One who could lead them to repentance. It is the sin of unbelief carried to the point of no return. The lesson says it cannot be forgiven, not because God's grace runs short, but because the man who persists in calling good evil has shut against himself the only door through which pardon comes. The troubled soul who fears having committed it shows by that very fear a tender conscience the Spirit has not abandoned, for the one who has truly rejected the Spirit no longer cares at all.

sa.prompt: What sign did Jesus refuse to give on demand, and what sign did He promise instead?
sa.model: When the scribes and Pharisees demanded a sign, Jesus refused to perform on command, calling them an evil and adulterous generation that seeks after a sign. He said no sign would be given except the sign of the prophet Jonah. For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the Son of Man would be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. The sign of Jonah points forward to His own death and resurrection, the one sign that settles everything, for as Jonah came up from the deep as from the grave, so the Son of Man would rise. He warned that the men of Nineveh, who repented at Jonah's preaching, would rise in judgment against that generation, for a greater than Jonah was there.

sa.prompt: Who did Jesus say are His true family, and how does this gather the unit's theme of mission and opposition?
sa.model: When told that His mother and brothers stood outside, Jesus stretched out His hand toward His disciples and said that whoever does the will of His Father in heaven is His brother and sister and mother. His true family is bound not by blood but by obedience to the Father. This gathers the whole theme of the unit, for these three chapters move on two tracks at once: the King's mission goes out as the Twelve are sent and the weary are invited, while opposition rises as cities refuse to repent and the Pharisees plot His death and slander the Spirit. The same light that draws some hardens others, and Jesus drew the line that there is no neutral ground before this King. Around Him, in the midst of rising opposition, a new family is forming of those who hear the will of God and do it.
